domain_label: Neural & Semantic Search (subdomain of Information Retrieval)
purpose: machine-readable expert system for designing embedding-based and learned retrieval (bi/cross-encoders, late interaction, ANN indexing, contrastive training, hybrid fusion, RAG, evaluation) as a fine-grained subdomain node in a knowledge-searcher KB for finding authoritative knowledge semantically
assumptions: no observed dataset, expert judgment, or experimental/benchmark evidence was supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
subdomain of information_retrieval_and_search_systems scoped to embedding-based and learned retrieval beyond lexical matching
scores are relative ordering priors for planning, not measured performance
consumed by a meta-KB knowledge searcher as one fine-grained subdomain node
exclusions: classical lexical-only retrieval internals (BM25 scoring math) except as a fusion/baseline component
general LLM pretraining and alignment beyond retrieval grounding
vector-database operational/infra details beyond index family and quantization choices
domain-specific corpora content; this KB models the retrieval method layer

glossary.definition: dual encoder embedding query and document independently for fast ANN retrieval
model jointly encoding query+document for high-precision reranking
approximate nearest neighbor structure for sublinear vector search
vector compression splitting dims into subvectors with learned codebooks
using other batch examples as negatives in contrastive training
high-scoring non-relevant document used to sharpen contrast
rank-based fusion combining rankings without score calibration
hypothetical document embedding: embed an LLM-generated answer to retrieve
retrieval-augmented generation grounding an LLM on retrieved evidence
cache keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact key

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for neural/semantic retrieval design, scoring, and risk; no observed or benchmark dataset supplied
grounding_limits: all scores are heuristic priors, not measured
no observed or experimentally validated labels permitted

nodes.definition: Define the semantic retrieval task, corpus, query distribution, latency/recall budget, and success metric before any model choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus size or query mix changes by >25%

pros.claim: Frames recall/latency tradeoff so downstream index and model choices are bounded
pros.example: fix nDCG@10 and p99<150ms before picking HNSW vs flat

cons.claim: Over-specification can prematurely exclude viable architectures
cons.example: locking single-vector before testing late interaction

acceptance_tests: task spec names corpus, query type, metric@k, latency budget
reviewer confirms metric matches business goal

nodes.definition: Select or fine-tune the contextual encoder (transformer) producing dense query/document vectors.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain vocabulary diverges from encoder pretraining

pros.claim: Contextual embeddings capture synonymy and polysemy lexical match misses
pros.example: 'java island' vs 'java language' separated by context

cons.claim: Encoder choice fixes dim and tokenizer, constraining the whole index

acceptance_tests: embedding model card records dim, pooling, normalization
spot-check nearest neighbors are semantically coherent

nodes.definition: Dual-encoder (DPR-style) that embeds query and document independently for fast vector search.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: held-out recall@100 drops below BM25 baseline

pros.claim: Independent encoding lets doc vectors be precomputed and ANN-indexed for sublinear search
pros.example: DPR retrieves over 21M passages in ms

cons.claim: No query-document interaction caps ceiling recall vs rerankers

acceptance_tests: bi-encoder beats BM25 baseline on held-out recall@100
query and doc encoders configured consistently

nodes.definition: Reranker that jointly encodes query+document pairs to score a small candidate set with full attention.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-stage candidate recall ceiling changes

pros.claim: Full cross-attention yields highest precision@k on the candidate set
pros.example: reranks top-100 to recover hard relevant docs

cons.claim: Quadratic per-pair cost forbids scanning the full corpus; needs a recall stage

failure_modes: latency blowup if candidate set too large
acceptance_tests: reranker improves nDCG@10 over first-stage order
p99 latency within budget at chosen candidate depth

nodes.definition: Multi-vector late-interaction (ColBERT) scoring via per-token MaxSim, balancing bi-encoder speed and cross-encoder quality.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: multi-vector index size exceeds storage budget

pros.claim: Token-level MaxSim recovers fine-grained match without full pair encoding
pros.example: ColBERTv2 nears cross-encoder quality at lower cost

cons.claim: Multi-vector storage explodes index size and needs residual compression

failure_modes: MaxSim latency at high token counts
acceptance_tests: late interaction beats single-vector recall at fixed latency
residual compression keeps index within budget

nodes.definition: Choose and configure an approximate nearest neighbor index family (HNSW, IVF) trading recall, latency, memory, build cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: exact-vs-ANN recall gap exceeds tolerance

pros.claim: ANN gives sublinear search enabling million-to-billion scale corpora
pros.example: HNSW M/efSearch tunes recall vs latency

cons.claim: Wrong index family or params silently degrades recall vs exact search

failure_modes: recall cliff from undersized graph degree
acceptance_tests: measured recall@k vs exact within target gap
p99 query latency within SLO at target QPS
revisit_triggers: latency SLO or QPS target changes

nodes.definition: Compress vectors via PQ/OPQ/scalar quantization or ScaNN anisotropic quantization to fit memory and speed scoring.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quantization recall loss exceeds tolerance

pros.claim: PQ/OPQ cut memory 8-32x enabling in-RAM billion-scale search
pros.example: OPQ rotation reduces quantization error before PQ

cons.claim: Aggressive compression loses recall; needs rerank/refine to recover
cons.example: raw PQ recall below flat without reordering

acceptance_tests: recall after quantization within tolerance of full precision

nodes.definition: Train embeddings with contrastive loss (InfoNCE) pulling positives together and pushing negatives apart.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: positive-pair definition or loss temperature changes

pros.claim: InfoNCE aligns the space with the retrieval objective directly
pros.example: temperature-scaled cosine sharpens separation

cons.claim: Sensitive to negatives and temperature; easy to train a degenerate space

failure_modes: false negatives in batch corrupt gradient
acceptance_tests: trained model improves recall vs untrained encoder

nodes.definition: Use other in-batch examples as negatives to cheaply scale contrastive contrast count per step.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: batch composition or dedup policy changes

pros.claim: Reuses batch examples as negatives, scaling contrast count for free
pros.example: large batches act like many negatives

cons.claim: Random in-batch negatives are mostly easy, capping discrimination
cons.example: easy negatives give weak gradient signal

acceptance_tests: in-batch negatives raise effective negative count

nodes.definition: Mine hard negatives (top BM25/ANN non-relevant docs) to sharpen the decision boundary.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-stage retriever or labels change

pros.claim: Hard negatives near the boundary drive the largest recall gains
pros.example: ANCE refreshes negatives from the live index

cons.claim: Unfiltered hard negatives can be unlabeled positives, poisoning training
cons.example: top-BM25 may be a true positive

acceptance_tests: denoised hard negatives improve recall over in-batch only

nodes.definition: Distill a cross-encoder/teacher's relevance scores into a bi-encoder student to lift recall at retrieval speed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher reranker or its calibration changes

pros.claim: Soft teacher labels transfer ranking knowledge a student learns at serving speed
pros.example: MarginMSE/KL distills cross-encoder into DPR

cons.claim: Student ceiling bounded by teacher quality and coverage

failure_modes: distribution gap between teacher and student inputs

nodes.definition: Combine lexical (BM25) and dense rankings via reciprocal rank fusion or score normalization for robustness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: relative strength of lexical vs dense signal shifts

pros.claim: RRF merges complementary signals, recovering exact-match cases dense misses
pros.example: RRF robust without score calibration

cons.claim: Naive score addition fails across incomparable score scales

acceptance_tests: hybrid beats best single retriever on held-out set
fusion handles out-of-vocab and exact-match queries

nodes.definition: Expand queries/documents (doc2query, HyDE) to bridge vocabulary gaps before or during retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: expansion generator or its prompt changes

pros.claim: doc2query/HyDE bridge vocabulary mismatch by generating bridging text
pros.example: HyDE embeds a hypothetical answer to retrieve

cons.claim: LLM-generated expansions can hallucinate, injecting drift or noise

acceptance_tests: expansion improves recall on vocabulary-gap queries

nodes.definition: Wire retrieved evidence into an LLM generation context with grounding, citation, and context-budget control.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: upstream retrieval quality or generation LLM changes

pros.claim: Grounding the LLM on retrieved evidence cuts hallucination and enables citation
pros.example: answers cite source passages

cons.claim: Garbage retrieval propagates into confident wrong answers

failure_modes: retrieval errors amplified by fluent generation
acceptance_tests: answers grounded in and cite retrieved passages
faithfulness eval passes vs no-context baseline

nodes.definition: Calibrate and threshold reranker scores so cutoff/abstain decisions are reliable across queries.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reranker version or query distribution changes

pros.claim: Calibrated scores make 'no good answer' and cutoff decisions trustworthy
pros.example: threshold abstains when top score low

cons.claim: Calibration drifts with query distribution and needs monitoring

nodes.definition: Cache answers/embeddings keyed by semantic similarity to cut latency and cost on near-duplicate queries.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: similarity threshold or corpus freshness changes

pros.claim: Similarity-keyed cache serves near-duplicate queries cheaply
pros.example: paraphrased FAQs hit the same cache entry

cons.claim: Loose similarity threshold serves wrong cached answers

failure_modes: false cache hit returns wrong answer
acceptance_tests: cache threshold tuned for precision/recall of hits
staleness TTL invalidates on corpus update

nodes.definition: Assess and improve out-of-domain/zero-shot retrieval transfer beyond the training distribution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deployment domain differs from training domain

pros.claim: Quantifies whether a retriever holds up off its training distribution
pros.example: strong in-domain models can lose to BM25 zero-shot

cons.claim: Zero-shot gains are uneven across domains and hard to guarantee

acceptance_tests: zero-shot performance measured on held-out domains
no catastrophic regression vs lexical baseline

nodes.definition: Evaluate retrieval/reranking on heterogeneous benchmarks (BEIR) and task-matched metrics for honest comparison.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation suite or target metric changes

pros.claim: BEIR's diverse tasks expose generalization a single dataset hides
pros.example: measures transfer across 18 datasets

cons.claim: Benchmark overfitting and metric mismatch mislead model selection
cons.example: chasing one metric harms real task

acceptance_tests: evaluation uses task-matched metric@k on held-out judgments
no train/test leakage with the benchmark

nodes.definition: Manage embedding model version changes that require full corpus re-embedding and index rebuild.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model version increments

pros.claim: Treats encoder change as a breaking migration preventing mixed-space search
pros.example: old and new vectors are not comparable

cons.claim: Re-embedding a large corpus is costly and high-risk if interrupted
cons.example: billion-doc reindex is expensive and slow

failure_modes: mixed embedding spaces silently corrupt similarity

nodes.definition: Build/maintain labeled relevance judgments and query sets that ground every retrieval metric and training signal.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: candidate pool or annotation policy changes

pros.claim: Trustworthy labels are the foundation for both training and honest evaluation
pros.example: pooled judgments power nDCG

cons.claim: Shallow pooling under-judges deep dense hits, biasing recall estimates
cons.example: unjudged relevant docs counted as wrong

acceptance_tests: judgments cover pooled candidates from all systems

edges.why_related: Task spec and budgets bound the encoder choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping framing picks an over/under-powered encoder
edges.example: latency budget rules out a 7B encoder
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; refit model to spec

edges.why_related: Recall/latency/memory budgets bound index family and params
edges.risk_of_conflict: unframed index misses recall or SLO

edges.why_related: Target metric defines which benchmark metric to optimize
Task and query distribution define the judgment query set
edges.example: query log sampled for judgment set
edges.resolution_rule: framing query mix dominates label sampling

edges.why_related: Bi-encoder is built from the chosen contextual encoder
edges.example: DPR towers use the selected checkpoint

edges.why_related: Late interaction reuses token embeddings from the encoder
Contrastive training fine-tunes the encoder weights
edges.risk_of_conflict: training before model fix wastes compute

edges.why_related: Cache keys are embeddings from the same encoder
Encoder vocabulary bounds how expansion text is embedded
edges.benefit_of_coupling: expansion must embed in same space
edges.example: HyDE text embedded by same encoder

edges.why_related: Reranker needs a candidate set from the bi-encoder first stage
edges.risk_of_conflict: reranking without recall stage cannot scale

edges.why_related: Doc vectors from the bi-encoder are what the index stores
Dense ranking input to fusion comes from the bi-encoder
edges.risk_of_conflict: no dense arm collapses to lexical only

edges.why_related: Single-vector vs multi-vector compete for the same retrieval slot
edges.risk_of_conflict: running both doubles cost without plan
edges.example: ColBERT vs DPR for the recall stage
edges.resolution_rule: pick by recall-per-byte budget; default single-vector unless quality gap justifies

edges.why_related: RAG context is the reranked top-k from the cross-encoder
Calibration operates on the cross-encoder scores
Distillation uses the cross-encoder as teacher
Multi-vector index needs residual compression to be viable
edges.resolution_rule: quantization required to deploy late interaction

edges.why_related: Quantization is configured within the chosen index family
edges.example: IVF-PQ pairs IVF cells with PQ codes

edges.why_related: Quantization recall loss can force index params to be retuned
edges.risk_of_conflict: silent recall loss if not fed back
edges.example: add reorder/refine after PQ drops recall
edges.resolution_rule: stop when recall within tolerance; max one retune loop

edges.why_related: In-batch negatives are a sampling strategy for the contrastive loss
edges.risk_of_conflict: no negative strategy starves the loss

edges.why_related: Hard negatives are added after in-batch baseline is established
edges.example: ANCE adds hard negs over in-batch start

edges.why_related: Mined negatives retrain and update the bi-encoder, which re-mines
edges.resolution_rule: stop on recall delta<threshold; cap mining rounds

edges.why_related: Distillation augments or follows contrastive training of the student
edges.risk_of_conflict: distilling an untrained student is unstable

edges.why_related: New hard negatives feed back into the contrastive objective
edges.resolution_rule: filter false negatives; stop when gain plateaus

edges.why_related: Fused robust ranking feeds the RAG candidate set
edges.example: RRF output reranked then sent to LLM

edges.why_related: Expansion changes the query/doc text the encoder embeds
edges.resolution_rule: raises recall; gate expansion to limit drift

edges.why_related: Expansion most helps the lexical arm, shifting fusion balance
Calibrated cutoffs decide what evidence (or abstain) reaches RAG
edges.example: abstain when no passage clears threshold
edges.resolution_rule: calibration gate precedes RAG context fill

edges.why_related: Distillation updates the bi-encoder student weights
edges.resolution_rule: improves recall; cap to avoid teacher-error overfit

edges.why_related: Index recall ceiling limits the evidence available to RAG
edges.risk_of_conflict: index recall cliff starves RAG silently
edges.resolution_rule: monitor index recall as RAG precondition

edges.why_related: Zero-shot claims are measured on out-of-domain benchmarks
Training distribution shapes zero-shot generalization
Benchmark metrics require relevance judgments
Labels bound which mined negatives are true negatives
edges.resolution_rule: use judgments to filter hard negatives

edges.why_related: Changing the encoder forces re-embedding and reindex
edges.resolution_rule: treat encoder change as breaking; full reindex

edges.why_related: Reindex migration rebuilds the ANN index
edges.resolution_rule: index rebuild is part of migration

edges.why_related: Eval results can trigger revisiting task framing/metric
edges.resolution_rule: stop when metric target met; cap reframes

edges.why_related: End-to-end RAG quality is checked after component eval
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping component eval hides root cause

conflict_axes.trigger: latency SLO conflicts with deeper reranking or multi-vector scoring
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: honor latency SLO from framing; raise recall only within budget via candidate depth tuning
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: p99 latency breach with recall below target
conflict_axes.example: reranking top-200 misses p99 budget; cut to top-50

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive quantization saves memory but loses recall
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: compress to memory budget but keep recall within tolerance via reorder/refine
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: recall loss exceeds tolerance after compression
conflict_axes.example: PQ-64 fits RAM but drops recall@10 5 points; add refine

conflict_axes.trigger: quality gap vs storage cost for the recall stage
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: default single-vector; adopt multi-vector only if quality gap justifies compressed storage cost
conflict_axes.example: ColBERT wins nDCG but 20x storage; choose by budget

conflict_axes.trigger: dense misses exact-match/out-of-vocab queries lexical catches
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prefer hybrid fusion over dense-only when query mix has exact-match or rare-term queries
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: dense-only regresses on exact-match query slice
conflict_axes.example: product-code queries fail dense; RRF with BM25 recovers

conflict_axes.trigger: LLM expansion lifts recall but injects hallucinated drift
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: allow expansion only when reranking/calibration filters injected drift and net precision holds
conflict_axes.example: HyDE adds recall but hallucinated entity hurts precision

conflict_axes.trigger: top retrieved negatives may be unlabeled true positives
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: filter mined negatives against judgments/teacher before use; labels dominate raw mining
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: training recall regresses after adding hard negatives
conflict_axes.example: top-BM25 negative is a true positive, poisoning the loss

conflict_axes.trigger: student gains speed but inherits teacher errors and ceiling
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: distill only from a validated teacher; keep teacher rerank for high-stakes queries
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: student error correlates with teacher error on key slice

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing in-domain recall can hurt out-of-domain transfer
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if deployment is multi-domain, weight zero-shot transfer over peak in-domain fit
conflict_axes.example: fine-tuned model beats in-domain but loses to BM25 zero-shot

conflict_axes.trigger: loose cache reuse vs stale or wrong cached answers
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tighten similarity threshold and invalidate on corpus/encoder change; correctness over hit rate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: cache false-hit serves an incorrect answer
conflict_axes.example: paraphrase hits stale cache after corpus update

edge_cases.failure_mode: similarity scores meaningless across mixed spaces
edge_cases.example: half corpus re-embedded then job crashed

edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check mined negatives against judgments/teacher scores

edge_cases.example: empty-recall query still fills the prompt

edge_cases.trigger: BM25 and cosine scores added without normalization
edge_cases.failure_mode: one signal dominates the fused ranking
edge_cases.detection_method: inspect fusion weight sensitivity on held-out set

edge_cases.example: hypothetical answer names a nonexistent product
edge_cases.detection_method: precision delta of expanded vs raw query

edge_cases.example: MS MARCO overlap with a BEIR subset
edge_cases.detection_method: train/test overlap hashing and dedup audit

edge_cases.trigger: similarity threshold too loose or corpus changed
edge_cases.failure_mode: serves stale or wrong cached answer

workflow.objective: Fix task, metric@k, latency/memory budget, query distribution
acceptance_tests: spec names metric@k, latency, corpus, query type
exit_criteria: task spec reviewed and frozen for draft
workflow.do_first_because: framing bounds every downstream model and index choice (highest coupling foundation)

workflow.objective: Assemble relevance judgments, splits, and benchmark plan
exit_criteria: eval harness reproduces a baseline metric
workflow.do_first_because: labels and leakage-free splits ground every later metric and training signal
encoder choice fixes vector space, dim, and tokenizer for all downstream stages
first-stage recall sets the ceiling for reranking and RAG
negatives and distillation drive the largest recall gains before indexing is locked

workflow.objective: Build and tune the ANN index with compression
acceptance_tests: ANN recall within gap of exact
exit_criteria: index recall and latency meet SLO
workflow.do_first_because: index recall and latency directly bound serving quality and cost

acceptance_tests: reranker lifts nDCG@10 over first stage
exit_criteria: rerank improves precision within latency budget
workflow.do_first_because: calibrated reranking decides what evidence reaches the generator

workflow.objective: Wire retrieval into RAG with caching
workflow.do_first_because: RAG is where retrieval errors become user-facing wrong answers

workflow.objective: Measure zero-shot transfer and end-to-end quality
acceptance_tests: no catastrophic zero-shot regression vs lexical
workflow.do_first_because: honest cross-domain measurement gates release and prevents overfit claims

workflow.objective: Lock release and define reindex/migration policy
workflow.do_first_because: encoder/index changes are irreversible migrations needing review before hard lock
